label: Figure 12.7: Monopoly versus perfect competition without economies of scale
alt: A single MC curve shared by perfect competition and monopoly, with perfect competition at price P1, output Q1, versus the profit-maximizing monopolist restricting output to Q2 and charging the higher price P2.
caption: Here monopoly and perfect competition share the identical cost curve, MC. Under perfect competition, equilibrium is where MC (= industry supply) meets D = AR, giving price P<sub>1</sub> and output Q<sub>1</sub>. The profit-maximizing monopolist instead produces where MC = MR, restricting output to the smaller Q<sub>2</sub> and charging the higher price P<sub>2</sub>. Without a cost advantage, monopoly produces less and charges more than perfect competition would for the identical cost structure.
